cards.explanation: The answer is bowing down. The LORD says, "they will come over in chains and bow down to you." They trudge behind, and I bet that's a long walk, friends. Then they confess that God is with you.

The answer is False. The LORD says they will confess, "God is indeed with you, and there is no other; there is no other God." Their own gods never come up in that confession. They point to the God who is with "you," and that's all.

The answer is together in disgrace. The verse says, "the makers of idols will depart together in disgrace." Together is the word the text uses, friends. It comes right after the line that they will all be put to shame and humiliated.

The answer is shame. The verse says, "you will not be put to shame or humiliated, to ages everlasting." In the verse before, the makers of idols depart in disgrace, but Israel's story is different. Israel will be saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation. That's a long time to be safe, friends.

The answer is to be inhabited. The verse says of the LORD that "He did not create it to be empty, but formed it to be inhabited…" The earth was made to have people living on it. Then the LORD speaks: "I am the LORD, and there is no other."
The answer is True. The LORD says, "I, the LORD, speak the truth; I say what is right." He also says He hasn't spoken in secret. I'd take that over a rumor from the group chat any day.

The answer is those who carry idols of wood. The LORD says, "Ignorant are those who carry idols of wood and pray to a god that cannot save." Those are the people He calls ignorant, friends. The verse says two things about them: they carry idols of wood, and they pray to a god that cannot save.

The answer is the LORD Himself. He asks, "Who foretold this long ago? Who announced it from ancient times?" Then He answers, "Was it not I, the LORD?" He sets it up like a challenge and then just answers it. Then He says there is no other God but Him.

The answer is True. The LORD calls Himself a righteous God and Savior when He says, "There is no other God but Me, a righteous God and Savior; there is none but Me." Righteous and a Savior, both in one breath, friends. He says it right after asking who foretold this long ago.

The answer is to all the ends of the earth. The LORD says, "Turn to Me and be saved, all the ends of the earth…" That's about as far as an invitation can go, friends. He gives His reason right away: "for I am God, and there is no other."

The answer is False. The LORD swears by Himself, "Every knee will bow before Me, every tongue will swear allegiance." That says every knee and every tongue. Jacob's descendants aren't the only ones in that sentence.

The answer is that righteousness and strength are in Him alone. The LORD says, "Surely they will say of Me, ‘In the LORD alone are righteousness and strength.’…" The word "alone" is doing the heavy lifting. That's what He says they will say of Him.
The answer is False. The text says, "All who rage against Him will come to Him and be put to shame." They don't stay far away. They come to Him.

The answer is exult. The last verse says, "In the LORD all descendants of Israel will be justified and will exult." Justified and exulting, friends. That's the end of the passage, and it ends with a celebration. I think a good celebration deserves a fresh batch of cookies.
